> Raw counts go into DESeq2. Never CPM, never logged. The method does its own
> normalisation and feeding it normalised data breaks it.
>
> Pi writes the code and you decide what it means. Ask it to use `d` and
> `metadata` from the setup chunk, and to put its code under the step you are
> working on.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(DESeq2)

source(here("R/count_tables.R"))

d <- read_counts("instructional")

# The grouping you built and saved in notebook 02. If it is not there yet, this
# stops with a clear message instead of a confusing one.
groups_file <- here("data/my_sample_groups.csv")
if (!file.exists(groups_file)) {
  stop("Could not find ", groups_file,
       "\nGo back to notebook 02, Exercise 2, step 5 and save your per-sample ",
       "table with the `community` column. Or rebuild it here: the Lactobacillus ",
       "fraction from the species table, split at 0.5.", call. = FALSE)
}
sample_groups <- read_csv(groups_file)

metadata <- d$metadata |> left_join(sample_groups, by = "sample_id")
```

```{r}
dplyr::count(metadata, time_point, community)
```

# Exercise 1: Test the gene table with a grouping from the species table

## Part 1 — Predict (no code)

**1. Testing 13,738 genes, how many get a raw p-value below 0.05 if nothing is truly different?**

- *Your answer:*

## Part 2 — Ask, look, decide

### Step 1: set up and run the test

Suggested request: *Using `d` and `metadata` from the setup chunk, keep only
the week 18 samples. Keep genes with a count of at least 10 in at least a
quarter of those samples. Run DESeq2 on the raw counts with `~ community` and
the contrast anaerobe against lactobacillus. Add gene symbols and names from
`d$gene_info`. Save the results table to `data/genes_by_community.csv` with the
columns `feature` (the Ensembl ID), `baseMean`, `log2FoldChange`, `lfcSE`,
`stat`, `pvalue`, `padj`, `symbol` and `gene_name`.*

Tomorrow's notebook reads that file.

- Samples in each group (37 and 120)? Genes tested (13,738)?
  - *Your answer:*
- Do the first five count-table columns match the first five `sample_id` values, in order?
  - *Your answer:*

```{r}
# Week 18 samples only (157 of the 471)
wk18 <- metadata |> filter(time_point == "week_18")

# Reorder the gene count COLUMNS to match the metadata ROWS, in order.
degenes <- d$genes[, wk18$sample_id, drop = FALSE]

# The sample-order check. DESeq2 matches columns to rows by position and
# never warns if they disagree, so we prove it here instead of hoping.
stopifnot(identical(colnames(degenes), wk18$sample_id))
data.frame(first_five_columns = colnames(degenes)[1:5],
           first_five_sample_ids = wk18$sample_id[1:5])

# Raw counts only: genes kept if they have >= 10 counts in at least a
# quarter of the 157 samples
keep <- rowSums(degenes >= 10) >= ncol(degenes) / 4

# Reference level first, so contrast anaerobe vs lactobacillus gives a
# POSITIVE log2FC = higher expression in ANAEROBE samples
wk18$community <- factor(wk18$community, levels = c("lactobacillus", "anaerobe"))
table(wk18$community)

col_df <- as.data.frame(wk18)
rownames(col_df) <- col_df$sample_id

dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = degenes[keep, ],
  colData   = col_df,
  design    = ~ community
)
dds <- DESeq(dds)

res <- results(dds,
               contrast = c("community", "anaerobe", "lactobacillus"),
               alpha = 0.05)

genes_by_community <- as.data.frame(res) |>
  rownames_to_column("feature") |>
  left_join(d$gene_info, by = c("feature" = "ensembl_gene_id")) |>
  select(feature, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj,
         symbol, gene_name)

write_csv(genes_by_community, here("data", "genes_by_community.csv"))

c(sum(!is.na(res$padj)),                                   # genes tested
  sum(genes_by_community$pvalue < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),     # raw p < 0.05
  sum(genes_by_community$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),       # FDR < 0.05
  sum(genes_by_community$padj < 0.05 &
        abs(genes_by_community$log2FoldChange) > 1, na.rm = TRUE)) # > 2-fold
```

### Step 3: one result, four plots

From here on, write your own requests. Volcano plot, MA plot, raw p-value
histogram with the no-difference line, boxplots of the top six genes by
community.

- Pi's explanation of the sign convention:
  - *Your answer:*
- Does every boxplot agree with the sign of its fold change?
  - *Your answer:*

```{r}
# ---- Independent check of the contrast DIRECTION ----
# The sign of log2FoldChange claims which group has the higher mean.
# Here we count the normalised reads per group directly and compare signs.
norm <- counts(dds, normalized = TRUE)

dir_check <- genes_by_community |>
  filter(!is.na(padj)) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  mutate(
    mean_anaerobe      = rowMeans(norm[feature, wk18$community == "anaerobe", drop = FALSE]),
    mean_lactobacillus = rowMeans(norm[feature, wk18$community == "lactobacillus", drop = FALSE]),
    higher_in = ifelse(mean_anaerobe > mean_lactobacillus, "anaerobe", "lactobacillus"),
    direction_agrees = (log2FoldChange > 0) == (mean_anaerobe > mean_lactobacillus)
  )
dir_check |> select(feature, symbol, log2FoldChange, mean_anaerobe,
                    mean_lactobacillus, higher_in, direction_agrees)

# TRUE for every top gene means: positive log2FC = higher in anaerobe
all(dir_check$direction_agrees)

# The single strongest gene as a picture: one point per sample
plotCounts(dds, gene = dir_check$feature[1], intgroup = "community")
```

```{r}
# ---- Four views of the result (Step 3) ----

# 1. Volcano: effect size (x) against significance (y).
#    Dashed lines: padj 0.05 (horizontal) and two-fold (vertical).
volcano_data <- genes_by_community |>
  filter(!is.na(padj)) |>
  mutate(
    minus_log10_padj = -log10(padj),
    direction = case_when(
      padj >= 0.05 ~ "not significant",
      log2FoldChange > 0 ~ "higher in anaerobe",
      TRUE ~ "higher in lactobacillus"
    )
  )

top10 <- volcano_data |> slice_min(padj, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE)

ggplot(volcano_data, aes(log2FoldChange, minus_log10_padj, colour = direction)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change  (positive = higher in anaerobe)",
       y = "-log10 adjusted p-value",
       colour = "Direction")

# 2. MA plot: mean expression (x) against fold change (y).
#    Genes now curving away at low counts are the shrunken-LFC story.
plotMA(res, alpha = 0.05)

# 3. Raw p-value histogram. The flat part is what a "no difference" null
#    looks like; the tower near 0 is the real signal standing on top of it.
ggplot(genes_by_community, aes(pvalue)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, colour = "white") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = sum(!is.na(genes_by_community$pvalue)) / 20,
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  labs(x = "raw p-value", y = "number of genes",
       subtitle = "Dashed line = what pure chance would give")

# 4. Boxplots of the six strongest genes, normalised counts, log scale.
top6 <- genes_by_community |>
  filter(!is.na(padj)) |>
  slice_min(padj, n = 6, with_ties = FALSE)

box_data <- norm[top6$feature, ] |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rownames_to_column("feature") |>
  pivot_longer(-feature, names_to = "sample_id", values_to = "norm_count") |>
  left_join(select(top6, feature, symbol), by = "feature") |>
  left_join(select(wk18, sample_id, community), by = "sample_id")

ggplot(box_data, aes(community, norm_count)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~symbol) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Community", y = "Normalised counts (log scale)")
```

### Step 4: cutoffs are choices

Genes passing at `padj` 0.01, 0.05, 0.1 crossed with fold change 0, 1.5, 2, 4.
Then the test with a looser (10%) and a stricter (50%) gene filter.

```{r}
# ---- Cutoff grid: the SAME result counted at 12 different cutoffs ----
cutoff_grid <- tidyr::crossing(
    padj_cut = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1),
    fc_cut   = c(0, 1.5, 2, 4)          # fold change cutoff, so 0 = none
  ) |>
  mutate(
    n_genes = purrr::map2_int(
      padj_cut, fc_cut,
      ~ sum(genes_by_community$padj < .x &
              abs(genes_by_community$log2FoldChange) > log2(.y),
            na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    fold_change = ifelse(fc_cut == 0, "none", paste0(fc_cut, "-fold"))
  ) |>
  select(fold_change, padj_cut, n_genes) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = padj_cut,
              values_from = n_genes,
              names_prefix = "padj ")
cutoff_grid
```

```{r}
# ---- Gene filter: rerun the whole test at two other filter strengths ----
# The default run used: >= 10 counts in >= 25% of the 157 samples.
run_with_filter <- function(frac) {
  keep_v <- rowSums(degenes >= 10) >= ncol(degenes) * frac
  dds_v <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
    countData = degenes[keep_v, ],
    colData   = col_df,
    design    = ~ community
  )
  dds_v <- DESeq(dds_v)
  res_v <- results(dds_v,
                   contrast = c("community", "anaerobe", "lactobacillus"),
                   alpha = 0.05)
  tibble(
    filter        = paste0("10+ counts in ", frac * 100, "% of samples"),
    genes_tested  = sum(!is.na(res_v$padj)),
    padj_lt_0.05  = sum(res_v$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    `padj & 2fold` = sum(res_v$padj < 0.05 & abs(res_v$log2FoldChange) > 1,
                          na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

filter_comparison <- bind_rows(
  run_with_filter(0.10),   # looser
  run_with_filter(0.25),   # the run we already did
  run_with_filter(0.50)    # stricter
)
filter_comparison
```

Top ten genes labelled, your own colours, direction in words under the x axis,
dashed cutoff lines, saved as a PNG.

```{r}
# ---- Polished volcano, also saved as a PNG for slides ----
p_volcano <- ggplot(volcano_data,
                    aes(log2FoldChange, minus_log10_padj, colour = direction)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    "higher in anaerobe"       = "#D55E00",
    "not significant"          = "grey75",
    "higher in lactobacillus"  = "#0072B2"
  )) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed") +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    data = top10,
    aes(label = coalesce(symbol, feature)),
    colour = "black", size = 3, max.overlaps = 20
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "\u2190 higher in LACTOBACILLUS   |   log2 fold change   |   higher in ANAEROBE \u2192"
  ) +
  labs(y = "-log10 adjusted p-value",
       colour = "Direction",
       title = "Gene expression by vaginal community, week 18",
       subtitle = "Dashed lines: FDR 0.05 and two-fold change") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)

fig_dir <- here("notebooks", "figures")
dir.create(fig_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "volcano_genes_by_community.png"),
       p_volcano, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 150)

p_volcano
```

Type `/new` in Pi before you start. Steps 3 and 5 each save a file that

## Part 1 — Predict (no code)

**1. Why can you not test the species table with the `community` column you built from it?**

**2. How many of the 220 species survive "present in at least 10% of samples"? How many of those are present in all 157 samples?**

**3. If any species are significant, will they be higher in preterm or in term?**

## Part 2 — Ask, look, decide

### Step 1: the default run

Suggested request: *Using `d` and `metadata` from the setup chunk, keep the
week 18 samples and the species present in at least 10% of them. Run DESeq2 on
the raw counts with `~ outcome` and the contrast preterm against term, with the
default settings. Add `Genus` and `Family` from `d$taxonomy`, and list the
significant species with their fold changes.*

- Species tested (53) and significant (19)? Do the names look like what you would expect?
  - *Your answer:*

```{r}
# ---- Exercise 2, Step 1: species table by outcome, default settings ----

# Week 18 samples again; species columns reordered to match metadata rows
species18 <- d$species[, wk18$sample_id, drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(identical(colnames(species18), wk18$sample_id))

# Keep species present (count > 0) in at least 10% of the 157 samples
keep_sp <- rowSums(species18 > 0) >= ncol(species18) * 0.10

# Reference = term, so POSITIVE log2FC = higher in PRETERM
wk18$outcome <- factor(wk18$outcome, levels = c("term", "preterm"))

col_out <- as.data.frame(wk18[, c("sample_id", "outcome")])
rownames(col_out) <- col_out$sample_id

dds_sp <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = species18[keep_sp, ],
  colData   = col_out,
  design    = ~ outcome
)
dds_sp <- DESeq(dds_sp)   # default size factors: median-of-ratios

res_sp <- results(dds_sp, contrast = c("outcome", "preterm", "term"),
                  alpha = 0.05)

species_by_outcome_default <- as.data.frame(res_sp) |>
  rownames_to_column("taxon") |>
  left_join(d$taxonomy |> select(taxon, Genus, Family), by = "taxon") |>
  arrange(padj)

write_csv(species_by_outcome_default,
          here("data", "species_by_outcome_default.csv"))

c(sum(keep_sp),                                                # species tested
  sum(!is.na(res_sp$padj)),                                    # survived DESeq2's independent filtering
  sum(species_by_outcome_default$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE))   # significant

species_by_outcome_default |>
  filter(padj < 0.05) |>
  select(taxon, Genus, Family, log2FoldChange, padj)
```

### Step 2: look behind it

Which species have no zero in any sample? Size factor against *L. iners* share,
and against library size, both on log scales.

- What are the size factors measuring?
  - *Your answer:*

- What are the size factors measuring?
  - *Your answer:*

```{r}
# ---- What did the default size factors actually track? ----

# Species with no zero in any of the 157 samples. These are the only species
# DESeq2's default size factor can use for every sample; a species with a
# zero in a sample is silently dropped from that sample's ratio.
kept_sp <- species18[keep_sp, ]
no_zero_names <- rownames(kept_sp)[rowSums(kept_sp == 0) == 0]
no_zero_names
length(no_zero_names)

# Each sample's size factor, next to its library size and L. iners share
sf_table <- tibble(
  sample_id    = names(sizeFactors(dds_sp)),
  size_factor  = as.numeric(sizeFactors(dds_sp)),
  library_size = colSums(species18)[sample_id],
  iners_share  = unname(kept_sp["lactobacillus_iners", sample_id]) / library_size
)

# Two correlations. If size factors tracked library size, the first would be
# near 1; if they are tracking composition instead, the second will be larger.
cor(sf_table$size_factor, sf_table$library_size, method = "spearman")
cor(sf_table$size_factor, sf_table$iners_share,  method = "spearman")

ggplot(sf_table, aes(library_size, size_factor)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Library size (total species reads, log)",
       y = "DESeq2 size factor (log)",
       subtitle = paste0("Spearman correlation: ",
                         round(cor(sf_table$size_factor, sf_table$library_size,
                                   method = "spearman"), 2)))

ggplot(sf_table, aes(iners_share, size_factor)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Lactobacillus iners share of library (log)",
       y = "DESeq2 size factor (log)",
       subtitle = paste0("Spearman correlation: ",
                         round(cor(sf_table$size_factor, sf_table$iners_share,
                                   method = "spearman"), 2)))
```
